name: Habitats and Conservation Funding Call
summary: Grants for river and lake habitat rehabilitation and conservation in the Republic of Ireland, including spawning enhancement, bank protection, fencing and invasive species control. Angling clubs, local groups and other third parties can apply.

steps: Discuss with the IFI district inspector or assistant and the Projects Office
Full application, if the EOI is accepted
IFI environmental and full application review

eligibility.rule: Holds a valid salmon or sea trout licence (SSTRCPF) or a Midland Fisheries permit (MFF)
For Midlands Fisheries Fund, carry out the project within the Midlands Fisheries Group permit area
Submit at most two Midland Fisheries Fund applications per organisation per year
Provide scientific justification if the project includes remedial works
Avoid double funding and disclose other State-sector funding sought or received for the project

documents: Photographs of the proposed site showing the issues before works
Confirmation of consultation with the National Barriers Mitigation Team for fish passage design projects

effort.quote: Applicants must engage with the relevant River Basin District inspector or assistant inspector and the Projects Office to discuss proposals before submitting an application (Appendix 2).

As part of a new two-step process, all applicants must firstly complete an 'Expression of Interest' application on Inland Fisheries Ireland's online grant management portal before 8:00pm on Thursday, December 10th 2026.

After the expression of interest has been completed, full applications must then be submitted to Inland Fisheries Ireland via the online grant management portal by 5:30 pm on Thursday, February 4th, 2027.
EOI's are preliminarily evaluated by the RBD and the Projects Office. Only successful proposals that meet the minimum criteria will be allowed to progress.

Applications are reviewed in accordance with the IFI Environmental Assessment Process (EAP). Inland Fisheries Ireland then reviews the full application and prioritises the project in line with fisheries objectives.

eligibility.quote: Valid licence number required when applying for SSTRCPF, Valid Permit number required when applying for MFF.
Projects can only be applied for within the Midlands Fisheries Group permit area
applications to this fund generally do not require match funding, but are limited to 2 applications per organisation per year
Where projects include remedial works, scientific justification will be required.

Double funding is prohibited. If the Project(s) receives or is seeking grant funding from any other State Sector sources, including Local Authority, under other schemes or programmes, this must be indicated in the application form.

co_finance.quote: Feasibility studies/development plans which lead to future projects under the above headings. To a maximum of 80% funding or €25,000 whichever is less).

after_award.quote: Drawdown of funds is also dependent on the provision of a completion report for the project.
Audits will be conducted over 5 years following the agreed completion of the project.
The project works will be inspected by Inland Fisheries Ireland staff to ensure all works are conducted in line with best practice and to the satisfaction of Inland Fisheries Ireland.

documents.quote: Photographs of the proposed site/s that illustrate all the elements of the project, Photographs should identify the issues before work is done.

An expression of interest (EOI) application will include a minor description of the project, the location, the aims and objectives, an outline budget and a proposed methodology describing how the projects will be delivered and managed.
For fish passage design projects, provide confirmation of consultation with the National Barriers Mitigation Team.
